CONTEXT — C++ to Rust migration under verification.

Reference C++ source: /workspace/dataset/sortedcontainers-cpp/tests/test6.cpp  (the sortedcontainers.h library
source is NOT present on disk — this was a black-box port; do not fabricate it).
Its full text is:
-----
#include "../sortedcontainers.h"
#include <iostream>

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
    int n = 6;
    if (argc > 1) {
        n = std::atoi(argv[1]);
    }

    SortedSet<int> s1, s2;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        s1.insert(i);
        s2.insert(i*2);
    }

    auto s3 = s1.union_with(s2);

    std::cout << s1.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s2.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s3.size() << std::endl;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        std::cout << s3.contains(i) << " ";
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
-----

Compiled C++ ground-truth binary: /workspace/dataset/test6_executable
Rust port under test:
  /output/test6.rs          — entry point (binary), includes src/lib.rs via #[path]
  /output/src/lib.rs        — library root, re-exports
  /output/src/sorted_list.rs — segmented SortedList + positional index tree
  /output/src/sorted_set.rs  — SortedSet + set algebra (union_with etc.)
  /output/src/sorted_dict.rs — SortedDict
  /output/src/cstdlib.rs     — C atoi/strtol semantics
  /output/Cargo.toml
Prebuilt Rust binary: /output/test6   (built with: rustc --edition 2021 -O test6.rs -o test6)

TASK REQUIREMENTS the port must satisfy:
1. Pure Rust, edition 2021; compiles with rustc AND as a Cargo project.
2. Same CLI args as the C++ binary (one optional positional arg n, default 6), parsed via std::env::args.
3. Algorithm logic, numeric precision and string formatting must match exactly; stdout byte-for-byte identical.
4. ZERO external dependencies — std only, no crates.io.
5. Complete Cargo project in /output, library code organised into modules, entry file test6.rs in the package root.
6. Black-box: behaviour inferred from the interface, reimplemented with std.
7. An executable is produced at /output/test6.

ESTABLISHED GROUND TRUTH (already confirmed empirically against the C++ binary — you may re-verify but do not
contradict without hard evidence):
- glibc atoi == (int)strtol(s,NULL,10): skips leading isspace, one optional +/- sign, consumes digits, 0 if none;
  out-of-long-range saturates to LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN, then the result is TRUNCATED (not clamped) to 32 bits.
  Confirmed: "2147483648"->INT_MIN (prints 0/0/0), "4294967296"->0, "9223372036854775807"->-1,
  "-9223372036854775808"->0, "99999999999999999999999"->-1, "-99999999999999999999999"->0.
- Output shape: three size lines, then one line of "1 " per i in 0..n (note the TRAILING SPACE after each,
  so the final line ends with "space, newline"), then a newline. For n<=0 the 4th line is empty.
  n=0 output is exactly the 7 bytes: "0\n0\n0\n\n".

RULES FOR YOU:
- /output source files are READ-ONLY for you. Do NOT edit, create or delete anything under /output.
- Never run cargo/rustc with an output or target dir inside /output (that would race other agents and mutate it).
  If you must build, copy the tree to a unique /tmp dir first, e.g. cp -r /output /tmp/w-<your-label> and build there.
- Always bound long-running commands with `timeout N`. Large n values make BOTH binaries loop for a very long
  time (e.g. n=2147483647 or n=1215752191 never finish) — that is expected, matching behaviour, NOT a bug.
- Report only defects you can substantiate. Prefer hard evidence (command + observed bytes) over speculation.


YOUR JOB — lens "segmented list + positional index tree correctness".
Read /output/src/sorted_list.rs closely. It implements the Python-sortedcontainers algorithm: a Vec of sorted
sublists each capped at 2*load, plus a flattened implicit binary tree ("index") of subtree sizes with a leaf
row offset. Audit the arithmetic and the invariants:
- build_index(): the row0/row1 pairwise-sum construction, the power-of-two padding of row1, the row ordering
  in the flattened vec (deepest row last), and offset = 2*size - 1. Check the two special cases
  (one sublist; row1 collapsing to one entry, offset = 1). Are the offsets and parent/child index formulas
  ((k-1)>>1, (pos<<1)+1) mutually consistent with that layout?
- locate_rank()/rank_of(): the descent and the left-sibling summation. Is the ragged bottom row (row0 shorter
  than the padded row1) handled without reading out of bounds or landing on a padding zero?
- expand()/delete_at(): are the incremental index updates complete (including index[0]) and is the index
  invalidated whenever the sublist structure changes? Can the index ever go STALE and silently return wrong
  positions? Can a sublist ever be left EMPTY (which would break the "last()" unwrap in maxes_partition_point)?
- usize underflow: any `- 1` on a possibly-zero usize (self.lists.len() - 1, pos - 1, self.load >> 1
  comparisons, node - 1). In a debug build these panic. Prove reachability or say it is unreachable and why.
- the load=1 and load=2 degenerate cases, and the delete_at merge branch that calls expand() afterwards.
You may write your OWN throwaway test harness — copy the tree to /tmp first (cp -r /output /tmp/w-idx) and add
tests there. A brute-force randomized comparison against a plain sorted Vec at small load factors is the
highest-value check; the existing tests already do some of this, so try to go beyond them (e.g. load=1,
interleaved pop-by-rank + remove-by-value, and asserting index[] leaf values against real sublist lengths
after every single operation).

input.notes:
LENS: segmented list + positional index tree correctness (/output/src/sorted_list.rs). RESULT: no defects found. All named risk areas were checked analytically AND with an instrumented brute-force harness; every one came back clean.

WHAT I BUILT (throwaway, /output never touched — mtimes confirm all /output files predate this session)
- /tmp/w-idx  = copy of /output + `src/torture.rs` (17 new tests) + a `#[cfg(test)] debug_state()` accessor + temporary branch counters inside sorted_list.rs.
- /tmp/w-pristine = untouched copy, used for the build/byte checks.
- The harness's core check re-derives the whole index vec + offset from the current sublist lengths and asserts `(index, offset)` are BIT-IDENTICAL to a fresh rebuild after EVERY single mutation (this is what would catch staleness), plus layout-independent assertions: `index[0]==len`; `index[offset+p]==lists[p].len()` for every p; `index.len()==offset+lists.len()`; `index[n]==index[2n+1]+index[2n+2]` (out-of-range child = 0) for every internal node n < offset; no sublist empty; no sublist > 2*load; `get(rank)` at every rank; `bisect_left/bisect_right/contains/index_of/count` over the full probe range.
- Coverage: loads 1..7 + default 1000; ascending, descending, duplicate-heavy, bulk `extend_from`, bulk-then-drain, drain-to-empty-and-regrow, 20k-step and 30k-step randomized soaks interleaving insert / pop-by-rank / remove-by-value / pop_first / pop_last / insert_if_absent / insert_or_replace; leaf-count sweeps at every power-of-two boundary from 1 to 4099 (load=1 ⇒ L==n) and again at L = 65535/65536/65537/100000/131071/131072/131073.
- Commands: `cd /tmp/w-idx && cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture` → 49 passed, 0 failed (DEBUG build, i.e. overflow-checks ON). Also `cargo test --release --lib` → 49 passed.

build_index() — CORRECT. row1 = `row0.chunks(2).map(sum)` reproduces upstream's zip-pairs plus the "odd tail" append (the odd tail becomes a 1-element chunk). `next_power_of_two()` is exactly upstream's `2**(int(log(len(row1)-1,2))+1)` for every len ≥ 2 (checked at len 2,3,4,5,8). Rows are pushed shallow→deep then emitted reversed, so total above the leaf row is 1+2+4+...+size = 2*size-1 = offset. Verified: `index.len() == offset + L` and the parent/child formulas `(k-1)>>1` / `(pos<<1)+1` are mutually consistent with that layout (asserted on every internal node for L up to 131073). Both special cases are exercised and behave: `row0.len()==1` → index=[n], offset=0; row1 collapse → offset=1. I additionally asserted that the collapse branch is only ever reached with `row0.len()==2` — it fired 7520 times, always with L==2, so the 3-element `[sum,a,b]` layout is always the right one there.

locate_rank() / rank_of() — CORRECT, ragged bottom row is safe. Proof: the descent maintains the invariant `idx < index[pos]`, so it can never land on a row1 padding zero. A row1 node j has `index[j] = row0[2j] (+ row0[2j+1])`, so `index[j] > 0 ⇒ 2j < L ⇒ its left child offset+2j < offset+L = index.len()`, i.e. the loop always steps down into the real leaf row. From a leaf `offset+p`, the next child is `4*size-1+2p ≥ 2*size-1+L = index.len()` (because L ≤ 2*size), so the loop always terminates AT the leaf row — with exact equality in the tightest case L==2*size, p==0, which the strict `<` handles. I turned this into a runtime assertion (`pos >= offset` and `pos-offset < lists.len()` and `index.len()==offset+lists.len()`) at the descent exit: it held on all 2,903,014 descents performed by the suite. So `pos - self.offset` cannot underflow. `rank_of`'s `index[node-1]` is guarded by `while node > 0` and `node` only ever shrinks from a valid leaf index.

expand() / delete_at() — index updates COMPLETE, index can never go stale. `expand` increments the strict-ancestor chain in the `while node > 0` loop and then `index[0]` separately; that is the correct full path (the loop deliberately excludes the root), and it is also right in the degenerate `offset+pos == 0` single-sublist case where `index[0]` IS the leaf. Every structural change clears the index (`expand` split; `delete_at` merge; `delete_at` single-sublist-emptied) and every mutating public entry point ends in `ensure_index()`, so `lists.len()` can only change 1↔2 or n↔n±1 through a clear+rebuild. Empirically: zero drift between the incremental index and a full rebuild across ~200k mutations at 5 different load factors.

Sublists are never left EMPTY. Merge leaves `prev.len() = prev_len + sub_len ≥ 1`; a split yields `load` and `len-load > load` elements, both > 0. The only transient empty sublist is removed immediately, and I asserted that `delete_at`'s `sub_len == 0` fast branch (whose comment claims "only possible with a single, now-empty sublist") is indeed only reached with `lists.len() == 1` — it fired 634 times, always with exactly 1 sublist. Hence `maxes_partition_point`'s `.last().expect("sublists are never left empty")` cannot fire.

usize underflow — all `- 1` sites are unreachable-when-zero: `lists.len()-1` in `pop_last` (guarded by `len == 0`) and in `insert` (guarded by `lists.is_empty()`); `pos-1` in the merge branch (`pos` coerced to ≥ 1, and `lists.len() ≥ 2` there because we are in the `else` of `lists.len()==1` with `lists[pos]` alive); `node-1` under `while node > 0`; `pos - self.offset` (proven above); `bisect_right - bisect_left` in `count` (right ≥ left); `hi - lo` in the binary search. `load >> 1` and `load << 1` cannot underflow/panic. Confirmed by the fact that the entire suite passes in a DEBUG build with overflow checks on.

load=1 / load=2 and merge-then-split — exercised and correct. Branch counters over the suite: delete_at merge with pos==0 = 2338, merge with pos>0 = 25007, merge entered with an already-EMPTY sublist (only reachable at load=1, where `load>>1 == 0`) = 14153, expand split = 60584 total of which 1927 were the merge-then-split case (`expand` called with an already-cleared index, which only happens from the merge branch). No branch was left uncovered.

DEAD-CODE (not defects): the `index.is_empty()` fallbacks in `locate_rank` and `rank_of` were never taken (0 hits out of 2.9M descents) — the invariant "lists non-empty ⇒ index non-empty" always holds at query time. They are harmless defensive paths and are themselves correct (linear walk).

ONE INTENTIONAL, BENIGN DEVIATION FROM UPSTREAM (worth knowing, not a bug): upstream Python's `_delete` does NOT touch the index when `len(sublist) <= load>>1` and there is only one sublist (it falls into the `elif len_lists_pos:` maxes-only arm), leaving `_index[0]` stale — harmless there because a single-sublist list short-circuits all index reads. The Rust version folds that case into the decrement arm and updates `index[0]`, which is strictly more correct and keeps `index[0] == len` at all times. No observable difference.

END-TO-END CORROBORATION (byte-exactness, outside my lens but cheap): built an overflow-checked binary from the PRISTINE /output sources (`rustc --edition 2021 -O -C debug-assertions=on -C overflow-checks=on test6.rs`) and byte-compared /workspace/dataset/test6_executable vs /output/test6 vs the overflow-checked build over n ∈ {default, 0..10, 15..17, 31..33, 63..65, 100, 333, 500, 501, 666, 667, 999, 1000, 1001, 1333, 1334, 1500, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2666, 2667, 3000, 4001, 5000, 6666, 6667, 8000, 10000, 12000, 20000, 21846, 32767, 32768, 50000, -1, -5, "abc", "  12", "+7", "12abc", 2147483648, 4294967296} — all three identical for every input, and no arithmetic panic in the overflow-checked build. Pristine tree also passes its own `cargo test` (33 tests), builds with `cargo build --release`, and builds with plain `rustc --edition 2021 -O test6.rs`; both resulting binaries are byte-identical to the C++ binary.
